# ui::ControlHeader

Header: `winui/ui/ControlHeader.hpp`.

The `Header` label an input control ([Slider](../controls/slider.md#uislider), [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox), [ToggleSwitch](../controls/toggle-switch.md#uitoggleswitch), [TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox), [NumberBox](../controls/number-box.md#uinumberbox), ...) carries above itself. It draws wrapping text in the primary text color, or in the disabled color while the control is disabled, takes no room while empty, and leaves a per-control gap below it.

It is not an [Element](element.md). The control owns one as a plain member and calls it from its own measure, arrange and render, so the element tree stays the same. [arrange()](#arrange) takes the header off the top of the control's rect and leaves the rest as the control's bounds, so hit tests, focus rings and popup anchors still cover only the control itself.

Example: 
```cpp
class LabeledThing final : public ui::Element
{
public:
    void set_header(std::string text)
    {
        if (header_.set_text(std::move(text)))
        {
            mark_dirty(ui::DirtyFlags::Layout | ui::DirtyFlags::Visual);
        }
    }

protected:
    ui::Size measure_override(ui::Size available, const ui::MeasureContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Size header = header_.measure(available.width, context);
        const ui::Size room   = ui::ControlHeader::below(available, header);
        const ui::Size body{120.0f, std::min(room.height, 32.0f)};
        return ui::ControlHeader::above(body, header);
    }
    void arrange_override(const ui::Rect&, const ui::ArrangeContext&) override
    {
        header_.arrange(*this); // bounds() is now the body's rect
    }
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Theme& theme = context.theme;
        header_.render(renderer, theme, /*enabled=*/true);
        renderer.fill_rounded_rect(bounds(), 4.0f, theme.colors().background); // the body
    }

private:
    ui::ControlHeader header_{4.0f}; // gap below the header, DIPs
};
```

## ControlHeader

```cpp
ControlHeader(float gap)
```

`gap` is the space in DIPs between the header and the control below it (4 for a [Slider](../controls/slider.md#uislider)). It applies only while the header has text.

## text

```cpp
const std::string& text() const
```

The header text; empty (the default) collapses the header entirely.

## set_text

```cpp
bool set_text(std::string text)
```

Returns whether the text changed, so the caller knows to mark itself dirty for layout and visuals, since the header's height depends on its text.

## empty

```cpp
bool empty() const
```

True while there is no text. The header then takes no room and draws nothing.

## measure

```cpp
Size measure(float available_width, const MeasureContext& context) const
```

The room the header takes above the control, in DIPs: its width, and its height plus the gap. Zero when empty. It wraps at `available_width` when that is bounded (> 0). [arrange()](#arrange) uses the height from the last call.

## arrange

```cpp
void arrange(Element& control)
```

Takes the header (as last measured) off the top of `control`'s bounds(), which are left as the control's own rect. Call it from the control's arrange_override(). A no-op while empty.

## render

```cpp
void render(Renderer& renderer, const Theme& theme, bool enabled) const
```

Draws the header where [arrange()](#arrange) put it, in the theme's disabled look while the control is disabled.

## below

```cpp
static Size below(Size available, Size header)
```

`available` with the header's height taken out, for measuring the control below it. An unbounded height stays unbounded.

## above

```cpp
static Size above(Size control, Size header)
```

The control's own desired size with the header stacked on top of it: the wider of the two, and the heights summed.
